pie.cook: Place the pie on a baking sheet on the lower oven rack to catch drips. Bake at {temp} for {time}, until the crust is deep golden and the filling is bubbling through the vents.
pie.check: The crust should be deep golden and the juices bubbling thickly through the vents. If the edges brown too quickly, cover them with strips of foil.
notes: Let the pie cool for at least 2 hours so the filling can set before slicing.
A smaller or deeper pie dish changes the time - start checking early.

recipes.name: Apple Pie
recipes.description: A double-crust pie with tender cinnamon apples and a flaky, buttery crust.

yield.note: Based on one 9 in (23 cm) double-crust pie.

less.note: Apples are naturally sweet and the cornstarch sets the filling, so about 25% less sugar still gives a juicy, set pie.

steps.title: Make the Crust
steps.text: Whisk the flour, salt and sugar. Cut in the cold butter with your fingertips or a pastry cutter until pea-sized pieces remain. Sprinkle in the ice water 1 tablespoon at a time, tossing, until the dough just holds together when squeezed.

steps.title: Chill the Dough
steps.text: Divide the dough into two discs (one slightly larger), wrap them and chill for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Make the Filling
steps.text: Toss the sliced apples with both sugars, the cornstarch, cinnamon and lemon juice until evenly coated.

steps.title: Assemble the Pie
steps.text: Roll out the larger disc and fit it into your pie dish ({pan}). Add the filling and dot with the butter. Roll out the second disc, lay it over the top, trim and crimp the edges, cut 4-5 steam vents and brush the top with the milk.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool the pie on a wire rack for at least 2 hours before slicing.

tips: Keep everything cold - cold butter and ice water make a flaky crust.
Mix a variety of apples (tart and sweet) for the best flavor and texture.
Do not skip the vents - they let steam escape so the crust stays crisp.

panOptions.text: 6-7 in / 15-18 cm pie dish - about 5 slices
two 9 in / 23 cm pie dishes, or one 9×13 in / 23×33 cm slab pie dish

recipes.name: Blueberry Pie
recipes.description: A juicy double-crust pie filled with sweet-tart blueberries.

yield.note: Based on one 9 in (23 cm) double-crust pie.

less.note: Blueberries are naturally sweet and the cornstarch sets the filling, so about 25% less sugar works; the pie will taste fruitier and a little tarter.
expectedChanges: Filling is tarter and more fruity

steps.title: Make the Crust
steps.text: Whisk the flour, salt and sugar. Cut in the cold butter with your fingertips or a pastry cutter until pea-sized pieces remain. Sprinkle in the ice water 1 tablespoon at a time, tossing, until the dough just holds together when squeezed.

steps.title: Chill the Dough
steps.text: Divide the dough into two discs (one slightly larger), wrap them and chill for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Make the Filling
steps.text: Gently toss the blueberries with the sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice and cinnamon until evenly coated.

steps.title: Assemble the Pie
steps.text: Roll out the larger disc and fit it into your pie dish ({pan}). Add the filling and dot with the butter. Roll out the second disc, lay it over the top, trim and crimp the edges, cut 4-5 steam vents and brush the top with the milk.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool the pie on a wire rack for at least 2 hours before slicing.

tips: Use the cornstarch exactly as written - blueberries release lots of juice.
Bake until you see thick bubbles - that means the cornstarch has set the filling.
Cool for at least 2 hours, or the filling will run.
